RagShortTexts: Fine fur clothing displays wealth and standing.
Acquisition, storage and repair add to clothing costs.

Variants.Content: Fur caps and coats combine warmth, wealth and ceremony. Species, condition and workmanship affect value. Keeping, repairing and giving furs express relationships; status also depends on person and occasion, not a cap alone.
Furs warm travelers but add weight and trouble when wet. A guard needs free movement and weapon handling rather than cumbersome display.
A fur gift signals patronage and creates expectations. Inspection and sound keeping ensure costly garments arrive as honor rather than spoiled goods.
Households balance selling fur for food against keeping warmth. Altering old garments costs work, and not everyone has another coat while one is repaired.
